I’ll recheck those pins at the end and condition any GO on final new-app validation. I’ll also use the xTS evidence skill to keep the conclusion bounded to Root’s single FS qualification run.

The completed receipt reports the new app validation as finished. In the source, timed writes proceed from the loop through checked flush/sync and close before reporting or verification. The output also labels the hardware gap separately from the 10 ms endpoints. I’m now checking handle lifetimes, error exits, and the claimed two-object build delta.

The independent hash audit matches the delivery claim: all 3343 compile commands agree after path normalization, and only `esp_spiflash.c.o` and `s31fsbench_main.c.o` differ from E97. The 3769 dependency hashes match the receipt; the other 20 application ELFs are unchanged.

The stream exercise uses eight handles in one task. It invalidates every reader before updates, checks changed bytes before writer fsync while peers remain open, and provides a bounded hold for Root’s resource snapshots.

I found no blocking code defect for the bounded trial. One reporting defect remains: a failed `qualify-clean` prints `retained=0` even when its guard preserves the files; Root must use the failure result and filesystem state. Also, the hold’s “8 windows / 32800 bytes” is an expected allocation label—stdio can fall back if promotion fails.

The saved 48 app cases, five timer-mock cases, and live-hold check pass. I’m doing the final pin recheck before writing the review.
